chunks: I was informed by Muhammad ibn Harun al-Zanjani in what he wrote to me. He said: We were told by Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam, that he said: We were told by Haitham, that he said: We were told by Yunus, from al-Hasan, that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family,

Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was brought to him, so he placed him on his lap. He urinated on him, so he took him and said: Do not interrupt my son. Then he called for water and poured it on him.
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad handle the urination of Imam Husayn on his lap?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, highlights the Prophet’s gentle demeanor and practical application of ritual purity (*taharah*) by allowing the child to finish naturally before cleansing. It serves as a key textual basis for the Shia juristic view that the urine of a pre-pubescent boy is not inherently impure (*najis*) but requires only rinsing, contrasting with the urine of a girl which necessitates washing. The incident underscores the Prophet’s affectionate leadership and the ease (*yusr*) he brought to domestic and ritual life.
